page: Vultr vhf-1c-2gb is an entry-tier virtual machine within the High Frequency Compute family. It features a single shared vCPU based on the Intel x86_64 architecture operating at 2.0 GHz, configured with 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory allocation is set at 2.0 GB of RAM. The server includes 64 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, one complimentary public IPv4 address, and does not contain a dedicated GPU accelerator.

Benchmark results reflect the limitations of a single shared core. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved 1266.88 in both single-core and multi-core evaluations, placing it in the lower percentiles relative to multi-core cloud instances. PassMark testing produced an overall CPU score of 2017.05, with 1681.75 for extended instructions and 638.11 for cryptographic operations. Memory throughput registered 11.09 GB/sec for large-block reads and 10.16 GB/sec for writes, while small cached reads reached 100.1 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 1.77 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.68 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. A bright spot in processing is single-threaded gzip compression, which achieved an average tier score of 24.19 GB/sec.

The shared CPU allocation and low memory ceiling introduce performance variability under sustained high loads. However, the integration of fast NVMe local storage provides solid I/O responsiveness relative to its resource footprint. This configuration is best suited for lightweight web serving, low-traffic API endpoints, dev/test environments, microservices, and small background utility scripts that do not require continuous multi-threaded compute.
